walkthrough:
Rearrange the equation to express $\tan x$:
$$3\sin x = -2\cos x \implies \tan x = -\frac{2}{3}$$
$$\text{Basic angle } \alpha = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \approx 33.69^\circ$$

Find the solution in the second quadrant ($90^\circ < x < 180^\circ$):
$$x_1 = 180^\circ - 33.69^\circ = 146.31^\circ \approx 146.3^\circ$$

Find the solution in the fourth quadrant ($270^\circ < x < 360^\circ$):
$$x_2 = 360^\circ - 33.69^\circ = 326.31^\circ \approx 326.3^\circ$$
$$\text{Solutions: } x = 146.3^\circ, \quad 326.3^\circ$$

hints: Sketch $y = 2\cos x$ from $(0,2)$ to $(360^\circ, 2)$ with amplitude 2.
Sketch $y = -3\sin x$ from $(0,0)$ through $(90^\circ, -3)$ to $(360^\circ, 0)$ with amplitude 3.
walkthrough:
Plot $y = 2\cos x$ over $[0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ with amplitude 2:
$$\text{Key Points: } (0^\circ, 2), \, (90^\circ, 0), \, (180^\circ, -2), \, (270^\circ, 0), \, (360^\circ, 2)$$

Plot $y = -3\sin x$ over $[0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ with amplitude 3 (inverted sine wave):
$$\text{Key Points: } (0^\circ, 0), \, (90^\circ, -3), \, (180^\circ, 0), \, (270^\circ, 3), \, (360^\circ, 0)$$
Ensure the curves intersect at $x \approx 146.3^\circ$ and $x \approx 326.3^\circ$, with $y = -3\sin x$ displaying a clearly larger amplitude than $y = 2\cos x$.

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Graphs: Sketches full cycle of $y=2\cos x$ (B1). Sketches inverted full cycle of $y=-3\sin x$ (B1). Shows larger amplitude on sine curve (B1).

hints: The inequality $2\cos x + 3\sin x > 0$ means $2\cos x > -3\sin x$.
From graph, cosine curve is above inverted sine curve on $[0^\circ, 146.3^\circ)$ and $(326.3^\circ, 360^\circ]$.
walkthrough:
Interpret $2\cos x + 3\sin x > 0$ as the region where $y = 2\cos x$ lies above $y = -3\sin x$:
$$2\cos x > -3\sin x$$

Read the intervals from the sketch using the intersection boundaries from part (i):
$$0^\circ \le x < 146.3^\circ \quad \text{or} \quad 326.3^\circ < x \le 360^\circ$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Inequalities: Identifies interval $0^\circ \le x < 146.3^\circ$ (B1ft). Identifies interval $326.3^\circ < x \le 360^\circ$ (B1ft).
